page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.medium is a compute-optimized instance featuring a single dedicated physical core powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Operating at 2.5 GHz on the arm64 architecture, this instance utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and includes 2.0 GB of system memory. The processor configuration provides 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the single-core configuration limits overall throughput. While the stress-ng single-core CPU performance registers in the average range at 1492.69, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks are constrained to the same level due to the single-vCPU limitation. Most performance metrics, including Geekbench scores, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput, fall into the lower percentile. For example, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 1.1 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 924.0.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6gn.medium offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated ARM64 compute resources without the overhead of shared-core credit systems. It is suitable for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, simple text processing, ARM64 software compilation testing, and small-scale utility tasks that do not require high memory capacity or multi-threaded execution.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.medium is a compute-optimized, arm64-based instance featuring a single dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 core running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it is equipped with 2.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU. Performance benchmarks show average single-core CPU capabilities with a stress-ng score of 1492.69, though overall multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics are constrained by the single-core architecture. This instance serves as a cost-efficient, dedicated entry point for lightweight ARM64 workloads, including basic web serving, text processing, and software compilation testing. It is highly suited for developers needing a dedicated, non-burstable environment for testing ARM-native applications without high resource overhead, delivering a balanced profile for low-intensity, single-threaded operations.
